# package cdcf

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/cdcf"
```

Package cdcf is the concise DCF of CiA 302-3: the binary form of a node configuration that a CANopen manager keeps in its object 0x1F22 (one DOMAIN sub-object per node) and writes to the node at boot-up.

A concise DCF is a little-endian UNSIGNED32 number of entries followed by the entries, each an UNSIGNED16 index, an UNSIGNED8 sub-index, an UNSIGNED32 data size and that many bytes of data (the value in the encoding of the object's data type). The entries are written to the node in the order they appear.

	entries, _ := cdcf.FromFile(dcf, 5)
	blob, _ := cdcf.Encode(entries)
	_ = managerDict.Set(0x1F22, 5, blob)

[Entries](#func-entries) extracts the configuration of a DCF (eds.File) as entries; [FromFile](#func-fromfile) also orders the PDO parameters in the sequence CiA 301 requires (invalidate the PDO, clear the mapping, write the mapping, set the number of entries, make the PDO valid), so that the result can be written as it is. [PDOSequence](#func-pdosequence) does that ordering for any entry list.

Sources: the format is that of Lely lely-core (co\_dev\_read\_dcf, co\_csdo\_dn\_dcf\_req and the dcfgen tool), CANopenNode and the CiA 302-3 object descriptions published by CiA members' device manuals.

```go
const (
	// IndexConciseDCF is the concise DCF of each node (ARRAY of DOMAIN,
	// sub-index = node-ID) in a CANopen manager.
	IndexConciseDCF uint16 = 0x1F22
	// IndexExpectedConfigDate is the expected configuration date of
	// each node (UNSIGNED32, days since 1984-01-01), compared with the
	// node's 0x1020 sub-index 1.
	IndexExpectedConfigDate uint16 = 0x1F26
	// IndexExpectedConfigTime is the expected configuration time of
	// each node (UNSIGNED32, ms after midnight), compared with the
	// node's 0x1020 sub-index 2.
	IndexExpectedConfigTime uint16 = 0x1F27
	// IndexVerifyConfiguration is a node's verify configuration object
	// (CiA 301): sub-index 1 configuration date, sub-index 2
	// configuration time.
	IndexVerifyConfiguration uint16 = 0x1020
)
```

### func Encode


Encode returns the concise DCF of entries. It fails only when an entry's data or the number of entries exceeds the UNSIGNED32 range.

Entry is one value to write into a node's dictionary.

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) ([]Entry, error)
```

Decode parses a concise DCF. An empty input is an empty configuration (an unset 0x1F22 sub-object); otherwise the input must hold exactly the number of entries its header announces, without trailing bytes. The entries' data are copies.

#### func Entries

```go
func Entries(f *eds.File, node canopen.NodeID) ([]Entry, error)
```

Entries returns the configuration a DCF holds for a node: every writable sub-object with a ParameterValue (without the "refuse write on download" object flag), in index order, with node-ID-relative values evaluated for node (0: the DCF's DeviceComissioning node-ID). For a PDO with any configured sub-object the whole communication and mapping parameter (every sub-object, current values) follows the other entries, so that a manager can apply the PDO as the DCF describes it. The PDO entries are in dictionary order: use [PDOSequence](#func-pdosequence) (or [FromFile](#func-fromfile)) to write them as they are.

#### func FromFile

```go
func FromFile(f *eds.File, node canopen.NodeID) ([]Entry, error)
```

FromFile returns the configuration a DCF holds for a node ([Entries](#func-entries)) with the PDO parameters in the sequence of [PDOSequence](#func-pdosequence): a concise DCF a manager can write entry by entry.

#### func PDOSequence

```go
func PDOSequence(entries []Entry) []Entry
```

PDOSequence returns entries with the PDO parameters (0x1400..0x1BFF) rewritten as the sequence CiA 301 requires to change a PDO, so that a node accepts them written one by one: the entries of other objects first, in their order; then, per PDO in the order the PDOs first appear, with the last value given for each sub-object:

 1. the COB-ID (sub-index 1) with bit 31 set (PDO invalid), when the entries set the COB-ID;
 2. the other communication parameters (sub-indices 2, 3, 5, 6; sub-index 0 and the compatibility entry 4 are dropped);
 3. when the entries set the number of mapped objects: 0, the mapping entries 1..n, then n (mapping entries above n are dropped); otherwise the mapping entries given;
 4. the COB-ID as given.
